title: Installing Node and Running Scripts
text: These questions check that you can install and run Node.js, use a terminal, and read Node's errors.

tasks.text: Your terminal's prompt is C:\Users\ava\Documents>. Your script is in C:\Users\ava\Documents\garden\report.js. Which command runs it?
A script copied from a web page stops with ReferenceError: document is not defined. Why?
choices: The code was written for a browser, and Node has no web page, so no document
document must be imported with npm

tasks.text: A script seems stuck in an infinite loop. How do you stop it?
An assistant's installation steps say to download node-v18.17.0. Why shouldn't you just use that version, and where should you get the version number?
tasks.answer: The assistant is remembering what was current when it learned; Node releases new versions regularly, so 18 may be outdated or unsupported. Get the current LTS from the official site, nodejs.org.

tasks.text: Explain this error, and how you'd fix it: Error: Cannot find module 'C:\Users\ben\harvest.js'
tasks.answer: Node looked for harvest.js in the current working directory, C:\Users\ben, and it isn't there. Move to the folder that contains the file with cd (or open that folder in VS Code and use its terminal), or type the full path.

tasks.text: Write a Node script (it can also run in the book's editor) with a function daysUntil(targetDay, today) that returns how many days from today (0 to 6) until the next targetDay, where both are getDay() numbers, and 0 if today is that day. Then write testDaysUntil, which logs daysUntil(6, 3), daysUntil(6, 6) and daysUntil(0, 5). (Expected: 3, 0, 2.)

Install Node and VS Code. Start a new chat with your updated learner profile, and ask for a Node script that prints each day of the coming week with its date, marking Saturday as a workday. (1) Paste the reply. (2) Run it in VS Code's terminal, and paste the output. (3) Introduce a typo on purpose, run it, and explain each part of the error message Node prints.
tasks.answer: Full credit: script runs with sensible output; the error message is explained (file and line, the pointer, the error type and message, the stack trace). Replies vary, so grade the reasoning.
